summary: 风暴过后发现的石墨最初被用来给羊做记号，后来成了笔芯。制笔工艺从包裹石墨发展到木壳和配方调整，不同的石墨与黏土配比形成了不同的笔迹。

paragraphs.brief: 然而，人们普遍承认，现代铅笔的历史始于16世纪，在英格兰西北部的坎伯兰乡村县山地。
sentences: Pencils have existed for millennia.
铅笔已经存在了几千年。

It is known that the ancient Egyptians, Greeks and Romans all used small pieces of metal as writing instruments, and that 14th-century European artists made pale grey drawings with thin rods of lead, silver or zinc.
众所周知，古埃及人、希腊人和罗马人都使用小块金属作为写作工具，14世纪的欧洲艺术家用薄薄的铅、银或锌棒制作了灰色的图画。
It is, however, generally accepted that the history of the modern pencil began in the 16th century, in the hilly, rural county of Cumberland in north-west England.
然而，人们普遍承认，现代铅笔的历史始于16世纪，在英格兰西北部的坎伯兰乡村县山地。

paragraphs.brief: 1565年前的某个时候县的Browshdale区发现了大量被称为石墨的软灰色矿藏
sentences: Some time before 1565, an enormous deposit of the soft, dark grey mineral now known as graphite was discovered in the Borrowdale district of the county.
1565年前的某个时候县的Browshdale区发现了大量被称为石墨的软灰色矿藏
Then, as now, Cumberland was a farming area, and the locals found the mineral useful for marking their sheep so they could identify the ones that belonged to them.
然后，像现在一样，坎伯兰是一个农地，当地人发现矿物质有用于标记他们的羊以便他们可以识别属于他们的羊。
It was thought to be a form of lead, and so was referred to as plumbago, a term deriving from the Latin name for that element.
据认为，这是一种铅形式，因此被称为Libabago，这个词源自该元素的拉丁语名称。

However, the mineral was later identified as a form of carbon, and in 1789 the German geologist Abraham Gottlob Werner renamed it graphite, a word based on the ancient Greek grapho, meaning ‘draw’ or ‘write’.
1789年，德国地质学家亚伯拉罕·戈特洛布·沃纳将石墨改名为“石墨”，该词以古希腊石墨为基础，意思是“绘制”或“写”。

paragraphs.brief: 在Browshdale发现的石墨非常稠密，很容易被锯成棍子，用于标记、写作或绘画。
sentences: The graphite found at Borrowdale was extremely dense and it could easily be sawn into sticks to be used for marking, writing or drawing.
在Browshdale发现的石墨非常稠密，很容易被锯成棍子，用于标记、写作或绘画。
But because graphite is also soft, it requires some form of encasement around it, and so the sticks were initially wrapped in string for stability and ease of use.
但是由于石墨也是软的，它需要某种形式的包围周围，所以木棍最初被包在绳子上以稳定和方便使用。
The news of the usefulness of these early pencils spread far and wide, attracting the attention of artists throughout Europe.
这些早期铅笔的有用性消息传播得非常广泛吸引了全欧洲艺术家的注意

paragraphs.brief: 英国政府很快意识到了特别是为了国防目的找到的宝物的价值因为石墨石墨被证明是
sentences: In England, the government soon realised the value of the Borrowdale find, particularly for national defence purposes, because graphite proved ideal for lining the moulds used in the making of cannon balls.
英国政府很快意识到了特别是为了国防目的找到的宝物的价值因为石墨石墨被证明是
The mines were therefore taken over by the government, which guarded and periodically flooded them to prevent theft.
因此，政府接管了这些地雷，并定期加以看守和淹没，以防止盗窃。
Because of this, there were occasions when supplies for use in pencils had to be smuggled out in secret.
因此，有时铅笔用具不得不秘密走私出来。
Nevertheless, England still became the centre of a thriving pencil-making industry.
然而，英格兰仍然是一个兴旺的铅笔制造工业的中心。

paragraphs.brief: 虽然世界上其他地方都存在石墨矿床，但这种矿床的纯度和质量与Lawrencedale石墨不同，必须粉碎成粉末才能消除杂质。
sentences: Although deposits of graphite existed in other parts of the world, they were not of the same exceptional purity and quality as Borrowdale graphite, and had to be crushed to a powder to get rid of the impurities.
虽然世界上其他地方都存在石墨矿床，但这种矿床的纯度和质量与Lawrencedale石墨不同，必须粉碎成粉末才能消除杂质。
England therefore continued to enjoy a monopoly on the production of pencils until a method of reconstituting the graphite powder could be found.
因此，英格兰继续垄断铅笔的生产，直到找到石墨粉重新粉末的重建方法。
English pencils continued to be made with sticks cut from pure Borrowdale graphite into the 1860s, after which the design was modified.
英国铅笔继续用棍子制成，从纯的Breeskidale石墨切成1860年代，此后对设计进行了修改。

The town of Keswick, close to the Cumberland graphite find, still manufactures pencils today, the factory also being the location of the Cumberland pencil museum Experimentation in pencil production was widespread across Europe during the 16th and 17th centuries.
坎伯兰石墨发现附近的Keswick镇今天仍然生产铅笔，该工厂也是坎伯兰铅笔博物馆铅笔生产实验的地点，在16世纪和17世纪期间，在欧洲各地广泛存在。
Around 1560, an Italian couple named Simonio and Lyndiana Bernacotti made what are probably the first blueprints for the modern, wood-encased pencil.
大约1560年，一对意大利夫妇名叫西蒙尼奥和林迪亚娜・贝纳科蒂制作了可能是第一个蓝图现代的木雕铅笔。
Their concept involved the hollowing out of a stick of juniper wood, and placing a stick of graphite inside.
他们的概念是用木棍挖空在里面放一块石墨

Shortly thereafter, a superior technique to that of the Bernacottis was adopted: two wooden halves were carved, a graphite stick inserted, and the halves then glued together — essentially the same method in use to this day.
不久之后，采用了比伯纳科蒂斯法更好的技术：雕刻了两根木头，插入了石墨棒，然后将两根木板粘在一起——基本上与今天所用的方法相同。

paragraphs.brief: 1662年在德国纽伦堡首次试图用粉状石墨制造石墨棒，使用石墨与硫和元素混合。
sentences: The first attempt to manufacture graphite sticks from powdered graphite was in Nuremberg, Germany, in 1662, using a mixture of graphite together with the elements sulphur and antimony.
1662年在德国纽伦堡首次试图用粉状石墨制造石墨棒，使用石墨与硫和元素混合。

paragraphs.brief: 大多数制造商使用石墨和粘土混在一起作为铅笔的核心。
sentences: Today, pencils are manufactured around the world, using graphite from a number of sources.
今天，铅笔是用若干来源的石墨制成的。
Most manufacturers use a mix of graphite and clay as the core of their pencils.
大多数制造商使用石墨和粘土混在一起作为铅笔的核心。
Each of these substances is ground into a fine powder, which goes on to be cleaned in order to remove any impurities.
每种物质都是粉末，再清洗，以去除任何杂质。
After the two types of powders have been dried, they are mixed together using water.
在两种粉末干涸后，它们使用水混合在一起。

The amount of clay added to the mixture depends on how hard the pencil is intended to be — higher proportions of clay will make the pencil harder — and the amount of time spent grinding the mixture determines the quality of the core.
混合物中添加的粘土数量取决于铅笔的用法——更高比例的粘土会使铅笔更难用——而混合物磨磨的时间决定了核心的质量。

The graphite-clay mixture is then shaped into long sticks, and after drying these are heated in a kiln to 1,200°C. In the next step in the process, the graphite-clay sticks are immersed in melted wax, which is absorbed into the mixture and helps to make it write more smoothly.
石墨板混合物随后形成长棒，在干燥后，在窑炉中加热至1,200°C。在工艺的下一步，石墨板棒浸入熔化的蜡中，被吸收到混合物中，有助于使其写作更加顺利。
In the next stage, the manufacturers use thin planks of cedar wood or juniper wood.
在下一阶段，制造商使用薄薄的雪松木板或柔性木板。
Several long parallel grooves are cut into the planks, and the graphite-clay sticks are inserted into these.
在木板上切开几个长长的平行槽，并在这些木板中插入石墨板条。
A second plank which has been prepared in the same way is then glued on top.
第二块木板是用同样的方式制作的，然后粘在上面。
The whole assembly is then cut into separate pencils.
然后将整个组装切成单独的铅笔。
The outside may then be varnished, retaining the natural colour of the wood, or painted in different colours.
然后，外部可以涂漆，保持木材的自然颜色，或涂上不同颜色。

items.en: was used by farmers in the area to indicate which ________ they owned
items.zh: 当地农民用石墨做记号，标明哪些________归自己所有。
items.why: 回到对应内容“然后，像现在一样，坎伯兰是一个农地，当地人发现矿物质有用于标记他们的羊以便他们可以识别属于他们的羊”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: was first believed to be a type of ________
items.zh: 人们起初以为石墨是________的一种。
items.why: 回到对应内容“据认为，这是一种铅形式，因此被称为Libabago，这个词源自该元素的拉丁语名称”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: was recognised by the English ________ as important in the manufacture of cannon balls
items.zh: 英格兰的________认识到，石墨对制造炮弹很重要。
items.why: 回到对应内容“英国政府很快意识到了特别是为了国防目的找到的宝物的价值因为石墨石墨被证明是”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: Borrowdale graphite was superior to all other forms of graphite.
items.zh: 莱克代尔石墨比其他所有石墨都好
items.why: 题干说 Borrowdale graphite was superior to all other forms of graphite,原文说其他地方的石墨没有 Borrowdale 石墨那样的 purity and quality,即 Borrowdale 更优质。两者一致，所以选 TRUE。

items.en: Pencil production in the Borrowdale area only lasted until the 1860s.
items.zh: 20世纪60年代，在Browkedale地区的铅笔生产一直持续到1860年代。
items.why: 题干说 only lasted until the 1860s,表示“只持续到19 世纪 60年代就停止"。但原文说 Keswick still manufactures pencils today,说明该地区附近今天仍生产铅笔。题干与原文矛盾，所以是 FALSE。

items.en: The Cumberland pencil museum contains examples of pencils from different European countries.
items.zh: 坎伯兰铅笔博物馆载有来自不同欧洲国家的铅笔实例。
items.why: 原文只说这个工厂是博物馆所在地，没有提到博物馆里面是否有 examples of pencils from different European countries。这是典型的“有相关名词，但具体内容未提及”,所以是 NOT GIVEN。

items.en: A technique which improved on the Bernacottis’ method of making pencils is still used now.
items.zh: 伯纳科蒂斯制作铅笔的方法有所改进，目前仍在使用。
items.why: 改良工艺把石墨夹在两半木片之间再粘合，原文说今天采用的仍基本是这一方法。

items.en: In 1662, manufacturers in Nuremberg made pencils with graphite imported from England.
items.zh: 1662年，纽伦堡的制造商用石墨从英国进口铅笔。
items.why: 原文确实提到 Nuremberg, 1662, graphite, 但没有说石墨是否 imported from England。由于“来源于英格兰” 这个信息没有出现，不能判断真伪，所以是 NOT GIVEN。

items.en: Graphite and clay are separately crushed to form powders, then ________ and dried
items.zh: 把石墨和黏土分别磨成粉，接着将粉末________，再烘干。
items.why: 回到对应内容“每种物质都是粉末，再清洗，以去除任何杂质”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: then, the sticks are dried, and ________
items.zh: 随后将笔芯棒晾干，再进行________处理。
items.why: 回到对应内容“石墨板混合物随后形成长棒，在干燥后，在窑炉中加热至1,200°C。在工艺的下一步，石墨板棒浸入熔化的蜡中，被吸收到混合物中，有助于使其写作更加顺利”，再按题干要求写出答案。
题干中的 dipped into 对应原文 immersed in,都是“浸入”。空格前是 into,答案直接填名词 wax。

items.en: the sticks are put into ________ in a wooden plank and another plank is fixed on top
items.zh: 将笔芯棒放进一块木板上的________里，再把另一块木板固定在上面。
items.why: 题干 put into…ina wooden plank 对应原文 inserted into these,而 these 指代前一句的 grooves。注意不能填 planks,因为条状物不是放进木板本身，而是放进木板里的凹槽。

items.zh: 最后，给铅笔________或涂上彩漆。
items.why: 题干 the pencils are…or painted 对应原文 may then be varnished…or painted。由于题干已给出 painted,所以空格填与 painted 并列的过去分词 varnished。

was thought to be a form of

in the manufacture of cannon balls
used in the making of cannon balls
a superior technique to that of the Bernacottis

points: 题干说 only lasted until the 1860s,表示“只持续到19 世纪 60年代就停止"。但原文说 Keswick still manufactures pencils today,说明该地区附近今天仍生产铅笔。题干与原文矛盾，所以是 FALSE。
题干中的 dipped into 对应原文 immersed in,都是“浸入”。空格前是 into,答案直接填名词 wax。
clauses: In England, the government soon realised the value of the Borrowdale find, particularly for national defence purposes, ….
连接词 because 引出“because graphite proved ideal for lining the moulds used in the making of cannon balls”，说明主句的原因关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 because 把这一层关系补进去。
…, they were not of the same exceptional purity and quality as Borrowdale graphite, and had to be crushed to a powder to get rid of the impurities.
连接词 although 引出“Although deposits of graphite existed in other parts of the world”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 although 把这一层关系补进去。
